<reflection>
- The first experiment resulted in very close NLL values for several models, with M7, M16, M17, M12, M11, and M14 emerging as the top candidates. 
- M7 (-20.156) is slightly preferred and features substrate activation (formation of a productive catS2 complex). The other top models feature irreversible catalyst deactivation induced by either substrate (M16, M11), product (M17, M12), or occurring spontaneously (M14).
- My aim to establish a baseline was achieved, and we now have a clear cluster of leading mechanisms that differ primarily in their deactivation triggers and substrate dependence.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To distinguish between substrate-induced deactivation (M16, M11), product-induced deactivation (M17, M12), and substrate activation without deactivation (M7), we need to decouple the concentrations of S and P. 
By running an experiment with a lower initial substrate concentration (S=0.5) and a high initial product concentration (P=0.5), we apply opposing pressures on the different deactivation pathways compared to Run 1 (S=1.0, P=0.0).
- For M17 and M12 (P-induced deactivation), the presence of P=0.5 at t=0 will cause immediate and rapid catalyst deactivation. The reaction will stall very early, resulting in almost no conversion of the remaining S.
- For M16 and M11 (S-induced deactivation), the lower initial S (0.5 vs 1.0) will decrease the rate of deactivation. The reaction will proceed to a higher relative conversion before stalling, showing less severe deactivation than in Run 1.
- For M7 (substrate activation, catS2 -> P + catS), the lower S will significantly reduce the initial rate due to the second-order dependence on S for forming the productive catS2 complex. However, because there is no irreversible deactivation, the reaction will not prematurely stall and will eventually reach full conversion.
This single experiment will cleanly separate the candidates based on whether the reaction stalls immediately, proceeds with reduced deactivation, or simply slows down without stalling.
</hypothesis>
